disclaimer: A starting point, not legal advice. Rules, forms and timelines differ by state and city, so confirm what applies with your ward office and local police station.

items.title: Written consent from the society or landowner
items.why: Most other applications ask for proof that you may use the site.

items.title: Police permission for the gathering
items.why: Police need to know the date, crowd size and organisers, and may set conditions.

items.title: Municipal permission for a pandal or temporary structure
items.appliesIf: If you put up a pandal, stage or tent, or use public land
items.why: Temporary structures and use of public land usually need ward-level approval.

items.title: Fire safety NOC or clearance
items.appliesIf: If you put up a pandal or tent, or cook on site
items.why: Pandals burn easily. Clearance usually covers exits, extinguishers and cooking away from the structure.

items.title: Traffic police permission
items.appliesIf: If you use a road or hold a procession
items.why: Blocking or diverting a road, or walking a route, needs a plan agreed in advance.

items.title: Loudspeaker permission
items.appliesIf: If you use loudspeakers or a sound system
items.why: The Noise Pollution Rules, 2000 require written permission, and generally bar loudspeakers from 10 PM to 6 AM, with limited local exceptions.

items.title: Temporary electricity connection
items.appliesIf: If you need power beyond the building's supply
items.why: Illegal tapping is a fire and legal risk. Use a licensed electrician.

items.title: Permission for fireworks
items.why: Only use licensed sellers. Local bans and court-ordered limits often apply.

items.title: Immersion site and timing
items.appliesIf: If an idol will be immersed
items.why: Cities name approved sites and time slots, and many have rules on idol materials.

items.title: Food safety registration
items.appliesIf: If you sell or serve food to the public
items.why: A caterer with a valid FSSAI licence is the simplest way to meet this. Ask for a copy.

items.title: Licence to play recorded music
items.appliesIf: If you play recorded music in public
items.why: Public performance of recorded music can need a copyright licence. Check what applies to your event.

items.title: Ambulance and nearest hospital arranged
items.why: Not usually a permit, but the first thing asked in an emergency.
